title: Semio Repository Test Protocol v2
description: 🧬️ Schema-first contract shared by the test coordinator, every native host and every external probe. v2 makes the unit of coverage `artifact × standard × smallest owning subset × runtime mutation × expected outcome class × fixture × subject implementation × platform`, replaces the single-projection result with a multi-artifact bundle, and requires a QUALIFYING third-party oracle for every mutation. Ticket 26/08/27/SUBSET-SCOPED-EXTERNAL-ORACLE-MUTATION-TESTING, baseline a8d1caf41f68204e73ff5e47ce40c5f543ed442d.

ArtifactRole.description: 🎭️ What one produced or expected file IS inside a bundle — `expected-step`, `actual-step`, `subject-mesh`. Roles are the join key between a fixture manifest, an adapter result and a comparison stage's inputs, so nothing in the pipeline addresses a file by path.

MutationOutcomeClass.description: 🎯️ The semantic class a fixture DECLARES for its mutation. A fixture that accepts any non-crash result measures nothing, so every fixture names exactly one of these.

EngineFamily.description: ⚙️ The exact-geometry or format kernel a reference actually sits on. Independence is accounted at the FAMILY level: two wrappers around one kernel are one oracle, not two.

QualifyingOracleKind.description: ✅️ The only kinds that can DISCHARGE a mutation's external-oracle requirement. `verified-native-second-implementation` is the one exception to "a second implementation never discharges", it exists ONLY for a format no third party can even in principle implement, and `nativeSecondImplementationBreaches` makes the claim EARNED rather than asserted — evidence object, native format, full capability coverage, a recorded no-third-party survey, a different implementation language, a specification source and at least one fixture vector.

SupplementalOracleKind.description: ➕️ Required supplements that can never substitute for a qualifying oracle. `cross-semio-implementation` names a second implementation written inside this repository — useful, and explicitly NOT independent evidence.

OracleLinkedPackage.description: 🧩️ One FURTHER third-party package a composed reference links beyond its primary one, pinned and licensed in its own right.

ProductionDebt.description: 🔒️ Pre-existing production reachability of a test-only package, recorded rather than hidden. Shrink-only: a path may leave this list, never join it.

OracleRegistryEntry.description: 📇️ One registered reference. `kind` decides whether it can discharge an external-oracle requirement at all; `engine` decides whether it is INDEPENDENT of the subject and of other oracles.

NativeSecondImplementationEvidence.description: 🌱️ What makes a `verified-native-second-implementation` claim EARNED rather than asserted. Required by `nativeSecondImplementationBreaches` whenever an entry carries that kind, and forbidden otherwise.

format.description: 🎯️ The `mutationManifests[].artifact` id this claims native status for — cross-checked against a real manifest this same contribution owns.

noThirdPartySurvey.description: 🔍️ The recorded negative search: what was checked, and why each candidate considered was declined.

specificationSource.description: 📖️ The written specification this was authored FROM — never the subject's own source.

ProbeRegistryEntry.description: 🔬️ One EXTERNAL measurement tool the comparison pipeline invokes. A probe computes; the framework only evaluates the typed JSON it emits. No geometry, no format parsing and no metric arithmetic may live in the orchestrator.

ProbeQualification.description: 🎓️ The recorded outcome of a qualification spike. A probe whose `status` is not `qualified` may be RUN, but no gate may claim its strongest guarantee — the canonical-STEP gate is the motivating case.

SubsetTarget.description: 🪆️ The SMALLEST semantic subset a mutation owns, plus the selector addressing the entity inside it. Wildcard and artifact-wide targets are unrepresentable here on purpose.

compound.description: 🧩️ For a cross-subset operation: the explicit typed compound. Declaring the compound is the ONLY way to span subsets — falling back to the whole artifact is a contract failure.

OracleRequirement.description: 🎯️ What a mutation needs from an external reference before it may be registered or released.

distinctEngineFamilies.description: ⚙️ How many INDEPENDENT engine families must supply this capability. Default 1; raise it where a single kernel ancestry would make the comparison circular.

ManifestMutation.description: 🦠️ One mutation as the DOMAIN owner declares it. This record is the single source that feeds both production registration metadata and the repository test catalog; there must never be two handwritten lists to reconcile.

subset.description: 🪆️ Overrides the manifest's own subset when this mutation is owned by a NARROWER one. Absent means the manifest subset owns it.

variant.description: 🦀️ The dispatch enum variant this row corresponds to, so runtime↔manifest equality is name-checked rather than order-checked.

normativeTopologyCounts.description: 🔢️ True only where exact face/edge/vertex counts are part of the mutation's SEMANTICS. Two valid kernels may split a periodic surface differently, so counts are never asserted globally.

MutationManifest.description: 🧬️ One owner's authoritative mutation inventory for one artifact/standard/subset. The contract phase requires `runtime inventory = manifest inventory = claimed test inventory`, exactly.

RuntimeMutationInventory.description: 🏭️ What PRODUCTION dispatch actually offers, emitted by the language-neutral bridge `listMutations(artifact, standard, subset)`. This file is generated by running production code, never by parsing source.

FixtureGenerator.description: 🏭️ Exactly how a third-party-generated fixture was produced, in enough detail to re-run it. A generated fixture with no reproducible generator record is a fixture nobody can audit.

FixtureManifest.description: 🧫️ One immutable fixture bundle. Updating a fixture creates a NEW identity and digest; the manifest is never edited in place.

target.description: 🎯️ The subset-scoped coordinates plus the mutation and the DECLARED outcome class.

family.description: 👪️ The fixture family this case belongs to (`spatial-relationship`, `shape-complexity`, `robustness`, `mechanical`, `failure`) — the sharding and reporting key that keeps a matrix from collapsing to artifact level.

ToleranceProfile.description: 📏️ Scale-relative tolerance policy. Effective tolerance is `max(absolute, relative × reference)`, so one profile serves micro-scale and large-coordinate fixtures without a per-fixture override.

ToleranceOverride.description: ⚠️ A fixture-level loosening of its profile. Every field is mandatory because an unexplained override turns a failure into a pass and nothing in the report would say so.

ComparisonAssertion.description: ⚖️ Declarative assertions evaluated against ONE probe's typed JSON output. Keys are probe-defined; the orchestrator only compares, never computes.

optional.description: 🚧️ A stage whose probe is not yet qualified. An optional stage RUNS and REPORTS, and its guarantee may not be claimed by any release gate.

ComparisonPipeline.description: ⚖️ An ordered, multi-artifact, externally-probed comparison. Replaces v1's single-projection profile for every case that produces more than one file or needs a measured metric.

referenceScale.description: 📐️ What `D` is when normalizing a length. `bounding-box-diagonal` is measured by a probe, never by the orchestrator.

ComparisonProfileSpec.description: ⚖️ The declarative structural profile a projection is compared under. Still the right tool for a single JSON/text/byte projection; a bundle uses a ComparisonPipeline instead.

FixtureRef.description: 🧫️ How a scenario ADDRESSES a fixture. v2 requires the manifest id alongside the digest so a run is keyed by reviewed provenance and not merely by bytes.

TestCasePlan.description: 📋️ The complete, serializable instruction one host receives. v2 adds the subset target, the mutation manifest digest and the comparison pipeline so a host can never widen its own scope.

ResultArtifact.description: 📦️ One file a host produced. `role` joins it to the fixture bundle and to every comparison stage.

TestResult.description: 📤️ One scenario × implementation × role execution. v2 returns an ARTIFACT BUNDLE plus a projection, so a BRep case can hand back STEP and a mesh without inventing a second protocol.

productionDispatch.description: 🏭️ Proof the subject reached PRODUCTION dispatch rather than replaying a committed vector. A subject result without it cannot count toward production-bridge coverage.

ProbeReport.description: 🔬️ The typed JSON one probe emits for one stage. `measurements` is probe-defined; the orchestrator evaluates the stage's assertions against it and computes nothing itself.

NoOracleDecision.description: 📇️ A recorded decision that a capability has no credible reference. v2 keeps it for NON-mutation capabilities only: a runtime mutation can never be discharged this way.

coversMutations.description: 🚫️ Structurally false. A mutation's external-oracle requirement is discharged only by a qualifying oracle.

RetentionClass.description: 🗄️ What a cached path IS, which decides when it may be removed. Failure evidence and pinned proof are never removed by routine stale cleanup.

RunLease.description: 🔐️ One agent's claim on one run directory. Clean and GC read this; an `active` lease is never reclaimed, and a stale one only after a documented timeout AND a process check.

RunManifest.description: 🗝️ Everything a reusable run result is keyed by. A changed tolerance profile must not reuse an earlier parity result, so the profile digest is part of the key rather than metadata beside it.

CoverageDimension.description: 📈️ Every dimension the release gate reads. A dimension that is not listed here cannot be gated, and a gate that reads nothing else cannot be satisfied by an aggregate.

CoverageRow.description: 📊️ One report row. The key is the FULL coordinate; sharding or reporting at artifact level is what this shape exists to prevent.

SchemaScopeId.description: 🏛️ The dotted id of an eligible scope owner, derived from its module `$id` path after `https://semio.tech/schema/`. Never derived by stripping emoji from a directory path.

SchemaExportId.description: 🎯️ A PascalCase key of the owning module's `$defs`, and the same-named entity in every format the module implements.

SchemaFormatId.description: 🔠️ A taxonomy `schemaFormats` key. The normative format of a `🧬️data` facet is `🔣️jsonschema`.

SchemaExportUri.description: 🔗️ `schema://<scope id>/<ExportId>` — the only way a fixture names the contract it is an example of. It resolves through the derived catalog; there is no nearest-parent search, no glob and no fixture-local fallback.

SchemaFixtureStage.description: 🪜️ The six stages every schema-bound fixture runs through, in order. A negative fixture names the stage it is supposed to fail at, so a case that starts failing EARLIER stops counting as the proof it was written to be.

SchemaDiagnosticCode.description: 🩺️ One code per distinguishable failure. "It did not resolve" is not actionable; "the catalog declares no scope s.writer.absent" is.

SchemaDiagnostic.description: 🩺️ One schema-contract finding, carrying everything needed to act on it and nothing inferred.

SchemaCatalogScope.description: 📚️ One scope's row in the derived catalog. `path` is the eligible owner directory; every `formats` value is a repository-relative file UNDER that directory.

SchemaCatalog.description: 📚️ The derived catalog: the single place `(scope id, export id, format id)` is answered from. Generated, never hand-edited.

SchemaFixtureTarget.description: 🎯️ What a fixture BINDS to: a named export of a scope, in one format. Never a file path.

SchemaStageExpectation.description: 🎯️ The stage, verdict and code a fixture asserts. A negative fixture that merely 'fails' measures nothing.

SchemaBoundFixture.description: 🧫️ One example that binds to a declared export. Exactly one of `data` (a case-relative file) and `inline` carries the subject.

SchemaStageOutcome.description: 🪜️ What one stage did. Every stage is reported — the ones after a failure as `skipped`, never omitted.

SchemaFixtureReport.description: 📤️ One schema-bound fixture's staged report — what `test schema` prints and a gate reads.

ContributionDirectoryOwnershipCases.description: 🧭️ The neutral owner-override vector every contribution-directory implementation is measured against. It lives here, in the owning module, because a case directory holds examples and never the contract they are examples of.

SchemaInvariantCases.description: 🧬️ The language-agnostic vector every implementation of the scope-owned schema contract is measured against: who may own a contract, where a definition may live, how `schema://` resolves, what a draft-07 validator must decide, and which stage a bound fixture fails at.
